"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 576: predict its typical value.

What the component does: very little. Its causal importance never passes the harvest
threshold (0 of 10M tokens; mean CI 9e-8), and switching it off moves the model's
next-token distribution by about 2e-6 nats per position. Its activation is a dense,
roughly bell-shaped value (mean 0.073, std 0.32) with no simple driver: the current
token, the previous or next token, a bag of the 16 preceding tokens, position in the
document, repetition, and the model's own next-token confidence each explain under 1%
of its variance on held-out text.

So this program predicts the component's mean activation at every position. It explains
no variance (activation recon is about 0), which is the honest result: nothing readable
captures its fluctuations. The mean keeps its average push on the residual stream.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.073  # mean over 2M training positions (0.0728); std 0.32


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Character-class predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 577.

The component's activation is a weak, diffuse signal: about 0.05 on most tokens,
with no clear trigger. Its activation is near 0 on the first token of each document,
somewhat higher on tokens made of digits, lower on CJK characters and on capitalised
words. This program predicts those class means and nothing finer.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

DOC_START = 0.0
DIGIT = 0.10
CJK = 0.01
CAPITAL = 0.025
OTHER = 0.055


def token_class(text):
    if regex.search(r"\p{Script=Han}", text):
        return CJK
    if text.strip().isdigit():
        return DIGIT
    if regex.fullmatch(r" ?\p{Lu}\p{Ll}+", text):
        return CAPITAL
    return OTHER


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    return carry, token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 579: a diffuse readout with no clean trigger.

What the component is: one rank-one direction written into the residual stream from
layer 15's MLP hidden state. Its activation averages about 0.02 with std 0.28. It almost
never passes the harvest's importance threshold (0 of 10M tokens), and its variance is
spread over thousands of hidden units, so no single concept accounts for it.

What this program does: the only tendency we found is by word class of the current
token. Tokens that sit inside a clause after a subject (copulas be/is/are/was/not,
possessives my/his/her/their/your/its, the clitic 's, "if") run a little above average.
Tokens that open a list or a noun phrase (A, one, two, this, The, or, also, commas,
newlines) run below it. Every other token gets the average. This explains well under 1%
of the variance; a token-identity table gets about 1.5% held out and is not worth its size.
"""

# Word classes, as the tokenizer decodes them (leading space included).
COPULA_AND_POSSESSIVE = {
    " is", " are", " was", " were", " be", " been", " not", " if",
    " my", " his", " her", " their", " your", " our", " its", "'s", "’s",
}
LIST_OR_NOUN_OPENER = {
    " A", " or", " also", " this", " one", " two", " The", " and", " new",
    ",", ",\n", "\n", "\n\n", " \n\n", " [",
}

READS = ()

ABOVE, BELOW, AVERAGE = 0.10, -0.03, 0.02  # mean activation of each class


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in COPULA_AND_POSSESSIVE:
        return carry, ABOVE
    if token in LIST_OR_NOUN_OPENER:
        return carry, BELOW
    return carry, AVERAGE

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 580 (the down_proj component 580), predicted from the text.

The component's activation is a dense, context-driven signal (std about 0.38) that no
token-level rule captures well. This program writes down the few regularities that show
up in its average behaviour, and nothing more:

- the first token of a document is essentially 0; the next few tokens sit low (about
  -0.13 at tokens 2 to 4), easing back toward the mean by about 12 tokens in;
- chat and markup control tokens (`<|im_end|>`, `</tool_call>`) push it clearly negative;
- a closing bracket or quote that ends a list item or a line (`),` `},` `])` `});`)
  pushes it mildly positive; other tokens, closers included, sit at the mean;
- bare newline and indentation tokens push it slightly positive.

Everything else takes the mean, about -0.01. On the eval rows this explains about 0.3%
of the variance (Pearson r about 0.06). The rules are a readable sketch of its average
behaviour, not a model of it: the activation's large swings depend on context that a
token-by-token reader cannot see.
"""
import re

READS = ()

MEAN = -0.01
CONTROL = re.compile(r"^(<\|| ?</)")
CLOSER = re.compile(r"[)\]}]")
CLOSER_ENDS_ITEM = re.compile(r"[)\]}]\s*[,;]?\s*\n|[)\]}][,;]$")
INDENT = re.compile(r"[ \t]{2,}$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label, position of the newest token within its document)
    doc, pos = carry if carry else (None, -1)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        doc, pos = prefix.document_ids[-1], -1
    pos += 1
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if pos == 0:
        v = 0.0
    elif pos == 1:
        v = -0.03
    elif pos < 12:
        v = -0.13 + 0.01 * (pos - 3)
    elif CONTROL.match(s):
        v = -0.25
    elif CLOSER.search(s):
        v = 0.08 if CLOSER_ENDS_ITEM.search(s) else MEAN
    elif s.strip() == "" and ("\n" in s or INDENT.match(s)):
        v = 0.07
    else:
        v = MEAN
    return (doc, pos), float(v)

"""Weak 'gloss context' proxy for the layers.15 MLP down_proj component 581.

The component reads mostly MLP hidden unit 581 of layer 15 (its V vector is about 0.68 of
its 0.93 norm on that unit). Its activation is a noisy signal, std ~0.37 at almost every
token. Token identity, the previous token, document, position and bag-of-context features
do not predict the bulk of it (held-out R^2 near 0), and no simple rule found does either.

Its largest positive values (up to ~17) often sit inside an English gloss or translation
of a foreign or quoted word or phrase ("... roughly translates to "Patterns"", "... the
word means "northern"", "... meaning “whole”"). This program predicts a small positive
value on tokens that come within a few tokens after a gloss cue word (mean, means, meaning,
translate, rendering, literally, gloss) in the same document, and 0 elsewhere. It captures
that tendency's sign and rough location only; it explains almost none of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

GLOSS_CUES = ("mean", "translat", "rendering", "literally", "gloss")
WINDOW = 6  # tokens back from the current one that may hold a cue
GLOSS_VALUE = 0.12  # mean activation on gloss-context tokens in the training sample


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids[-(WINDOW + 1):]
    words = prefix.token_strings[-(WINDOW + 1):]
    current = docs[-1]
    hit = any(
        doc == current and any(cue in word.lower() for cue in GLOSS_CUES)
        for doc, word in zip(docs, words)
    )
    return carry, GLOSS_VALUE if hit else 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP component 582 (down_proj): a biography-versus-personality feature.

What it does, in plain terms: it is positive in the opening of an encyclopedia-style
biography, where the model is about to name a nationality or an occupation, e.g.
"Name (born September 21, 1982) is [an] American politician". It is largest on the
date dash inside the birth/death parenthesis, then on "an", and on nationality words in
that header; "a", "is" and "was" there are weaker. Its output runs against trait words:
when it is negative, the logit lens raises words such as talent, charisma, personality,
traits and charm, so the program is negative on those words themselves. Everywhere else
it sits near a small positive baseline (the component's mean).

The values are a hand-set table of the strongest cases, fitted to the activations on
1024 training rows. They capture only a small part of the variance (about 0.3% on eval):
most of the component's variance is diffuse, spread over many ordinary tokens, and is
not tied to any word, phrase or position that I could find.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

BASELINE = 0.06
NATIONALITIES = frozenset(
    """american british english irish scottish welsh french german italian spanish
    portuguese dutch swiss swedish norwegian danish finnish polish russian soviet
    ukrainian czech hungarian romanian greek turkish israeli iranian egyptian chinese
    japanese korean indian pakistani thai vietnamese indonesian filipino australian
    canadian mexican brazilian argentine colombian cuban nigerian kenyan african""".split()
)
TRAIT_WORDS = frozenset(
    """personality personalities character traits trait talent talents talented skill
    skills ability abilities capable strength strengths weakness weaknesses qualities
    quality charisma charismatic charm charming genius gift gifted leader leadership
    shy introverted extroverted outgoing friendly kind caring honest honesty lazy
    confident insecure jealous passionate passion creative intelligent smart funny
    humble generous loyal patient patience aggressive anxious nervous emotional
    sensitive cruel gentle compassionate supportive respectful responsible reliable
    motivated motivation enthusiastic dedicated dedication curious afraid brave courage
    ambitious arrogant selfish rude polite nice natural""".split()
)
YEAR_OR_DAY = re.compile(r"\d+")
WINDOW = 14


def _doc_window(prefix):
    """The current document's last WINDOW tokens (lower-cased, stripped), newest last."""
    ids, t = prefix.document_ids, prefix.position
    j = t
    while j > 0 and ids[j - 1] == ids[t] and t - j < WINDOW:
        j -= 1
    return [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[j : t + 1]]


def _in_birth_header(win):
    """A parenthesis opened before a date, or the word 'born', within the window."""
    if "born" in win:
        return True
    return any(
        w == "(" and any(YEAR_OR_DAY.fullmatch(x) for x in win[k + 1 : k + 4])
        for k, w in enumerate(win)
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    win = _doc_window(prefix)
    cur = win[-1]
    value = BASELINE
    if cur in TRAIT_WORDS:
        value = -0.4
    if _in_birth_header(win):
        if cur == "–":
            value = 3.0
        elif cur in ("an", "a", "is", "was"):
            value = 0.5
        elif cur in NATIONALITIES:
            value = 1.3
    return carry, float(value)

"""End-of-document detector: layers.15.mlp.down_proj, component 583.

The component is strongly negative on the document separator <|endoftext|> (about -10.6)
and small everywhere else. On ordinary tokens it sits near zero, with a typical value of
about -0.1 to -0.3 and noisy fluctuations of about 0.7 that no simple rule explains.
Among ordinary tokens it is a little more negative when the token contains a newline,
and a little less negative when the token starts with a space.

The program predicts the large negative value on the newest token if it is the separator,
and otherwise the small value for its surface form. It reads only the newest token, so it
keeps no state between positions.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"
EOT_ACTIVATION = -10.6  # mean activation on the end-of-text token
# mean activation on other tokens, keyed by (has a newline, starts with a space)
OTHER = {(False, False): -0.16, (False, True): -0.09, (True, False): -0.32, (True, True): -0.28}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == END_OF_TEXT:
        return carry, EOT_ACTIVATION
    return carry, OTHER[("\n" in token, token.startswith(" "))]

"""Predicts component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:584 as its typical value, a constant.

What the component is: one rank-one direction on the output of layer 15's MLP down
projection. Across training text its activation is a diffuse, noise-like quantity
(mean ~0.008, std ~0.29, almost all within +/-1), and it is almost never important:
its causal importance averages 5e-8 and it never passes the 0.1 harvest threshold.

- Small hand-picked word classes (time units like "hours"/"days" negative, "after",

So no short, conceptual rule captures it. The program predicts the activation's mean,
0.008, everywhere; its effect on the model matches switching the component off.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()
MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.008


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """This component's activation at the newest position: its mean, a constant."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Nothing to run: the program is a constant. Predicting the mean leaves the output
    # essentially unchanged, as switching this component off does (KL about 1e-6 nats).
    print("constant", MEAN_ACTIVATION)

"""Predict L15 MLP down_proj component 585 from the word just read.

This component writes a small, diffuse signal into the residual stream. Almost no
surface feature explains its size, so this program only captures the few word
classes where its average value visibly moves:

- Adversative "but" / "However" (sentence- or clause-initial or mid-clause): clearly negative.
- Demonstratives "this" / "these": negative.
- Additive or causal connectives "also", "because", "since", and sentence starts
  "It", "There", "They": mildly positive.
- Everything else sits at the component's usual slight negative offset.
- The first token of each document (and of the packed row) is near zero.

It explains well under 1% of the variance; the rest is not captured by any simple rule.
"""

READS = ()

ADVERSATIVE = {" but", " But", "But", " However", "However"}
DEMONSTRATIVE = {" this", " these"}
ADDITIVE_CAUSAL = {" also", " because", " since", " It", " There", " They"}

BASE = -0.03
DOC_START = 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or docs[t] != docs[t - 1]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    word = tokens[t]
    if word in ADVERSATIVE:
        value = -0.4
    elif word in DEMONSTRATIVE:
        value = -0.25
    elif word in ADDITIVE_CAUSAL:
        value = 0.14
    else:
        value = BASE
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 586.

What it does, in plain terms: it fires on the shell chaining token " &&" when the
command before it is `cd <directory>`, as in `cd /testbed && npm test`. There it
reads about +3 (up to about +8). On other " &&" tokens it reads a little above zero,
and on every other token it stays near zero.

The rest of its variance is diffuse: about +/-0.35 on ordinary tokens, depending on
context in ways no token list captures, so this program predicts 0 there.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# A `cd <path>` immediately before the token: the path is one run of non-space text.
CD_BEFORE_AND = re.compile(r"\bcd\s+[^\s;&|]*$")

CD_AND_VALUE = 3.2  # mean activation on " &&" that follows `cd <path>`
OTHER_AND_VALUE = 0.3  # mean activation on any other " &&"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] != " &&":
        return carry, 0.0
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    before = text[:-3] if text.endswith(" &&") else text
    if CD_BEFORE_AND.search(before):
        return carry, CD_AND_VALUE
    return carry, OTHER_AND_VALUE

"""Introducer punctuation: colons, the word "by", and assignment "=".

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:587 is mostly quiet, but it
fires on tokens that set up a value, list, agent or explanation to come next:

- a colon (":" or the full-width "：") is the strongest trigger: about 6 when it is
  the first colon in the last 200 tokens of its document, about 4 when another colon
  occurred there (repeated colons fire less), and about 3 when it follows a digit
  (times, ratios, line numbers);
- other colon-bearing tokens (":\\n", "):", '":', ":\\n\\n") fire about 2;
- the preposition "by" (" by", " By") fires about 3.8, as in "passed by", "divide by";
- " =" fires about 1.3 on average (more in code than in maths).

Everything else predicts 0. The weights are the means of those groups on training
text. The rule explains about a fifth of the variance: the component's background
noise on ordinary tokens (std about 0.8) is not captured by any readable rule.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

COLONS = (":", "：")  # ASCII and full-width colon
WINDOW = 200  # tokens over which a repeated colon is damped


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: (document, position) of the last colon in this document, or None
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    doc, pos = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.position
    last = carry if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else None
    if tok in COLONS:
        after_digit = pos > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().isdigit()
        repeated = last is not None and pos - last[1] <= WINDOW
        value = 3.0 if after_digit else 4.0 if repeated else 6.1
        return (doc, pos), value
    if any(c in tok for c in COLONS):
        return last, 2.0
    if tok.lower() == "by":
        return last, 3.8
    if tok == "=":
        return last, 1.3
    return last, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 588: a diffuse, mostly-slightly-negative feature.

What it is, as measured: the component's activation is (MLP hidden . V_c) * |U_c|. About
half of its variance is one hidden unit of layer 15's MLP (unit 588), which is a
context-dependent feature. Its value is NOT explained by the current token, the previous
token or two, character classes in a window, position in the document or line, repeats of
earlier tokens, or the model's own entropy or confidence. It is mostly a small negative
number (mean about -0.06, spread about 0.4), with occasional positive peaks in citation,
name and year contexts, and negative dips in URL and email fragments.

Since no readable rule was found that predicts it, this program predicts the component's
typical value everywhere. Its variance explained is about zero on eval; switching the
component off and predicting its mean have almost the same effect on the model's output.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_ACTIVATION = -0.057
"""The component's mean activation over the eval rows."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return None, TYPICAL_ACTIVATION

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:589 (a single MLP hidden unit's worth of output).

What it does: it fires on words that introduce a conclusion in reasoning text, such as
"so", "therefore", "thus", "hence", "then", "implies", "means" and "⇒". Those are the
positions where a deduction from the preceding statement is about to be written out. The
activation is strongest on such words after a stated fact in mathematical working, and
near zero everywhere else. Most of the component's variance is NOT explained by this rule:
its activation is mostly small, context-dependent noise on ordinary tokens.

This program predicts a fixed positive value on conclusion words and 0 elsewhere.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

CONCLUSION_WORDS = frozenset(
    {"so", "therefore", "thus", "hence", "then", "implies", "means", "⇒"}
)
CONCLUSION_VALUE = 0.7


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, CONCLUSION_VALUE if word in CONCLUSION_WORDS else 0.0

"""Predicts layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 590 as its typical value, everywhere.

What this component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. Its activation
is (MLP hidden vector . V_590) * ||U_590||. About a quarter of its weight sits on one
hidden unit (unit 590 of that MLP), and the rest is spread thinly over the other ~6000
units, so there is no single neuron or concept it reads.

What we checked, on about 4000 training rows: token identity, token type (words, digits,
punctuation, CJK, newlines), position in document, whether a token or bigram repeats earlier
text, and document-level averages. None of these explains more than about 1% of the
activation's variance (held-out). Its activation is dense, roughly symmetric and
context-dependent, with a mean of about 0.06 and standard deviation 0.32. Its causal
importance is essentially zero everywhere, so switching it off barely changes the model.

So the program predicts the mean activation at every position. It explains none of the
variance, and it is the honest baseline: no simple readable rule was found that does better.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.058


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """This component's activation at the newest position: its mean value."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 591: a near-constant, nearly unpredictable write.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP output projection. It reads
the MLP hidden vector through a direction V (about a quarter of whose energy sits on
hidden unit 591 itself) and writes along U, with ||U|| about 1.9. Its activation
(h . V) * ||U|| is roughly symmetric around 0, with std about 0.33 and mean about 0.017.

What this program does: it predicts the component's mean activation at every position.

Why nothing better is offered: across 4.2M training positions, no readable feature from
the token stream explains the activation. The token identity, the previous token, the
position within the document, and the document's own average each explain about 0 to 4%
of its variance, and held-out tables give R^2 of about 0. The component is also
causally negligible: switching it off changes the next-token KL by about 1.4e-6 nats.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Mean activation over 4.2M training positions (about 0.0167).
MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.017


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # Constant prediction: needs no state and reads no tokens.
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Predict this MLP unit-direction's activation from whether the newest token is a number.

Component: layers.15.mlp.down_proj, direction 592. Its activation is a projection of the
layer-15 MLP hidden state, dominated by hidden unit 592 (about a fifth of its variance).
That unit leans positive on digits and some words (e.g. '5', '2', 'Check', 'Template')
and negative on many identifier and word fragments (e.g. '_b', 'zam', 'Entry', '/workspace').
Across tokens, the activation is only weakly tied to the token itself: a lookup table of
token means explains about 2% of its variance, and simple token classes explain almost none.

So the program is a two-level guess: digits sit slightly above the average, everything else
sits at the average.
"""

import re

READS = ()

DIGIT_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\s?\d+")
DIGIT_MEAN = 0.068   # mean activation on digit tokens in the sample
OTHER_MEAN = 0.037   # mean activation on all other tokens in the sample


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = DIGIT_MEAN if DIGIT_TOKEN.fullmatch(token) else OTHER_MEAN
    return carry, value

"""Predicts layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 593 from the words around each token.

What the component reads: a diffuse direction in layer 15's MLP hidden state. Its value is
mostly a small, noisy number near zero, with clear positive bumps in two places:

1. Conclusion connectives that open a step of reasoning: "Thus", "Therefore", "So",
   "Hence", "Then", "Consequently" (and lowercase forms). These are the strongest and most consistent.
2. Code: statement-opening words ("const", "var", "let", "return", "int", ...) and the
   indentation run that starts a line, but only when the surrounding text is dense with
   code punctuation (`{ } ; = ( ) < >`). Indentation in prose does nothing.

Everything else is near zero, in prose and code alike. Position in the document, line
length and token identity beyond these words add little, so the program ignores them.

Prediction = 1.5 * connective + 0.75 * code-word + 2.4 * (indent run * code density in the
last 40 tokens of the same document) + 0.02.
"""

READS = ()

CONNECTIVES = {"thus", "therefore", "so", "hence", "then", "consequently"}
CODE_WORDS = {"const", "var", "let", "return", "int", "get", "set", "create", "public",
              "await", "compute", "assert", "find"}
CODE_CHARS = set("{};=()<>")
WINDOW = 40


def _is_code_token(text):
    return any(ch in CODE_CHARS for ch in text)


def _is_indent_run(text):
    return text.strip() == "" and len(text) > 0 and "\n" not in text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The same-document tokens of the last WINDOW positions, ending at the current token.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    texts = []
    for text, label in zip(prefix.token_strings[-WINDOW:], prefix.document_ids[-WINDOW:]):
        if label == doc:
            texts.append(text)
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = current.strip().lower()

    density = sum(_is_code_token(t) for t in texts) / max(1, len(texts))
    value = 0.02
    if word in CONNECTIVES:
        value += 1.5
    if word in CODE_WORDS:
        value += 0.75
    if _is_indent_run(current):
        value += 2.4 * density
    return carry, float(value)

"""Weak token-class rule for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:596.

The component's activation is a diffuse signal: its average is about 0.037, and
it varies from token to token with standard deviation 0.31. Token class explains
almost none of that. The rule below predicts each token's class average, measured
on training text. Newlines and CJK or whitespace tokens sit slightly above average,
and punctuation and digits slightly below. At the first token of a row, where the
component is essentially zero, it predicts zero.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

CLASS_MEAN = {
    "newline": 0.079,
    "han": 0.054,
    "ws": 0.052,
    "word": 0.040,
    "partial": 0.042,
    "digit": 0.029,
    "other": 0.029,
    "punct": 0.025,
}


def token_class(text):

that unit), scaled by a fixed norm. Most of the time it sits near zero; it is a rare,
large spike that the rest of the model reads. Simple token features explain little of
its value, but one thing it tracks well is copying: how long a stretch of text ending
here already appeared earlier in the same document. On new text it sits near a small
baseline; the longer the current text repeats an earlier passage token for token (a
repeated line, a copied list, a repeated phrase), the higher it goes, leveling off
around a copy of 64 tokens. Line breaks and punctuation sit a little above words.

The program keeps each document's tokens. At each token it finds the longest run of
tokens ending here that also occurs earlier in the document (counting up to CAP), and
predicts BASE + QUAD * run**2 for runs of 2 or more, plus DELIM_BONUS on line breaks
and punctuation. It is a rough, conceptual fit: it explains about 3-4% of the variance.

READS = ()

CAP = 64           # longest copied run counted; the response levels off here
BASE = 0.036       # typical value on new text
QUAD = 0.00043     # growth with the copied run's length, (run ** 2)
DELIM_BONUS = 0.067
CANDIDATES = 8     # earlier places with the same bigram to check, most recent first


def _is_delim(s):
    # Line breaks and punctuation: the tokens that sit a little higher.
    t = s.strip()
    return "\n" in s or (t != "" and all(not c.isalnum() for c in t))

    hist, index = carry["hist"], carry["index"]
    hist.append(tok)
    i = len(hist) - 1
    run = 0
    if i >= 1:
        key = (hist[i - 1], hist[i])

        for e in index.get(key, [])[-CANDIDATES:]:

    return carry, value

What it is: about three quarters of this component's direction is a single hidden unit
of layer 15's MLP (unit 620), so its activation is that unit's value, scaled.

What it responds to, in plain terms: the binary operator of an arithmetic or algebra
expression (+ - * / ^ =, or < >) when it comes right after an operand (a number or a
single letter) and sits inside an open parenthesis, as in "(8 - h/(-" or "((-25)/(-10))".

formula-heavy the document has been so far, measured as the share of operator, number
and single-letter tokens so far. Everything else is predicted as 0.

mathematical text are not captured. Tuned on about 4000 training rows, this rule
explains about 1% of the activation's variance (r about 0.12).

from collections.abc import Mapping

# Arithmetic and comparison operators, possibly with spaces around them.
OPERATOR = re.compile(r"\s*[+\-*/^=<>]+\s*")
# A number or a single letter (a variable), possibly with spaces around it.
OPERAND = re.compile(r"\s*([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?|[A-Za-z])\s*")

    # formula tokens so far, all tokens so far). A new document resets it.

    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    is_operator = bool(OPERATOR.fullmatch(text))
    is_operand = bool(OPERAND.fullmatch(text))

    n_all += 1

    value = 0.0

        formula_share = n_math / (n_all + 10)
        value = 0.5 + 6 * formula_share

RUN_OF_SPACES = re.compile(r"\s{8,}")  # deep indentation in code

activation has mean about -0.047 and spread about 0.25 and is almost never large in

LATER = -0.04  # everything after

    its class (digit, letter, punctuation, space), or the token before it. Token-identity
    tables explain almost none of the variance.

    in a row, and attention resets at each document start):

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

FIRST_TOKEN = 0.0  # document's first token: component is silent
SECOND_TOKEN = -0.16  # document's second token: small negative mean
LATER_TOKEN = 0.01  # all later tokens: small positive mean


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
